title: Irish Wristwatch
subtitle: R, W & SH Combo
description: This exercise combines three demanding sounds — /r/, /w/, and /ʃ/ (SH) — in tight consonant clusters. The phrase 'Irish wristwatch' is widely considered one of the hardest single-phrase tongue twisters in English.
tip: Slow down to half speed first and nail each consonant before increasing pace. The transition from /r/ to /ʃ/ inside 'wristwatch' is the hardest part — give each sound its full shape.
phrases: An Irish wristwatch, a Swiss wristwatch.
She wore a Swiss wristwatch on her right wrist.
Which wristwatch is a Swiss wristwatch?
Around the rugged rocks the ragged rascal ran.
Whether the weather be fine or whether the weather be not, we'll weather the weather whatever the weather, whether we like it or not.
